newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian c.banker says T-bill yields to fall.
newsitem.headline: Russian c.banker says T-bill yields to fall.

text.p: Russian Treasury bill yields, which fell to a record low average 49.63 percent on six-month paper at an auction on Wednesday, are set to fall further as the amount of investment from non-residents builds up, a senior central bank official said on Wednesday.
First deputy chairman Sergei Aleksashenko told Reuters non-residents had bid "several hundred million dollars" at Wednesday's auction.
"Our talks show that the process of non-residents coming in will continue at the same stormy rate, and the yield will fall," Aleksashenko said.
He said heavy demand by foreigners was a major reason why the auction yield had fallen below 50 percent for the first time.
Russia introduced a new system for foreigners to buy and trade government securities in mid-August.

Under this scheme non-residents can open special "S" accounts with designated Russian banks, and use these accounts to buy government securities at auction and buy and sell them in the secondary market.
But bankers said the new system was poorly marketed at first, and a few weeks ago central bank officials were complaining that most of the banks designated to operate "S" accounts were inactive.
But bankers said interest in the "S" account system has picked up in the last week or so.
Aleksashenko said T-bils were also benefiting from Russia's better than expected credit ratings announced on Monday, which had led to a sharp rise in the price of dollar-denominated MinFin bonds.

"There are very many non-residents, lots of demand. With the announcement of Russia's rating and the rise in MinFin prices, non-residents have decided to invest more heavily in rouble denominated government securities, Aleksashenko said.

Dealers said another reason for strong non-resident demand at today's auction was the central bank's announcement on Monday that it was cutting the effective guaranteed dollar yield on T-bills payable to non-residents using the "S" account.

From October 16 this guaranteed yield, controlled by the central bank through the forward rates which non-residents must use to buy foreign currency when repatriating their investments, will fall to 16 percent from 19 percent.
Total demand at the auction of 10 trillion roubles of paper was 15.92 trillion roubles ($2.94 billion).
